1|# Quillon Orbital Works: company, private tool "Keel", and internal dashboard (SPEC, draft)
2|
3|Status: **draft for the user's review** (2026-10-28). Written by Claude (plan/spec role). To be built by **Muse Code**
4|after the user approves. Nothing here is a real company: "Quillon Orbital Works" was checked with a web search on
5|2026-10-28 and no company of that name was found. Every page must show "Fictional company, made for the Forge demo".
6|
7|## 1. Why this exists
8|Forge must prove that a small private model (Muse Glimmer 30B) can learn a company tool that **no AI has seen on the
9|internet**. CadQuery is public, so both models already knew it. Keel is a new, private tool with its own names, units
10|convention and company tables. The only ways to learn it are the company manual or Forge training.
11|Keel compiles to CadQuery internally, so the existing exact referee (`experiments/first-test/checks.py`: one solid,
12|bbox, volume, area, centre of mass, overlap mismatch ≤ 0.2%) still judges every answer.
13|
14|## 2. The company (story shown in the dashboard)
15|- **Quillon Orbital Works**: builds structural parts for small satellites (brackets, mounting plates, panel frames,
16|  standoffs, harness clips) for its smallsat bus **"Petrel"** (programmes Petrel-1, Petrel-2).
17|- Designs are **export-controlled** (fictional "QX-2" control level): they may not be sent to cloud AI. That is why
18|  the AI design assistant runs on one in-house GPU ("on-prem"), which is the Forge story.
19|- Small team (fictional): Structures, Avionics Integration, Quality. Engineers file **design requests** like
20|  "BRK-0412: base plate 60 × 40 × 4, four KF-M4 clearance holes 6 mm in from each corner, north wall 25 high".
21|
22|## 3. The private tool: Keel (Python library `keel`)
23|Design goals: (a) clearly different from CadQuery (names, datum, tables), so knowing CadQuery is not enough;
24|(b) small and fully documented in the manual; (c) every Keel program becomes exactly one CadQuery solid;
25|(d) deterministic, no randomness.
26|
27|### 3.1 Company conventions (the "unwritten rules" a new engineer must learn)
28|- Units are millimetres. **Datum = the part's lower-left-bottom corner** at (0,0,0). +X = "east", +Y = "north",
29|  +Z = "up". Nothing is centred unless the call says so.
30|- Edges of the base stock are named **north, south, east, west**.
31|- Holes use **company fastener codes**, never raw diameters (table KF below).
32|- "Standard wall" thickness = **2.5 mm**; "standard fillet" = **1.0 mm** (used when a request says "standard").
33|- Part numbers: BRK- (bracket), PLT- (plate), FRM- (frame), STD- (standoff), CLP- (clip).
34|
35|### 3.2 Fastener table KF (company table; values are the exact diameters the referee uses)
36|| Code | Clearance hole Ø | Counterbore Ø × depth |
37||---|---|---|
38|| KF-M2 | 2.4 | 4.4 × 2.0 |
39|| KF-M3 | 3.4 | 6.5 × 3.0 |
40|| KF-M4 | 4.5 | 8.0 × 4.0 |
41|| KF-M5 | 5.5 | 10.0 × 5.0 |
42|| KF-M6 | 6.6 | 11.0 × 6.0 |
43|Suffix `-CB` = counterbored from the top face (e.g. `KF-M4-CB`).
44|
45|### 3.3 API (first version; Muse Code may propose changes in its report, not silently)
46|```python
47|import keel
48|p = keel.part("BRK-0412", material="AL6061")       # material is metadata only
49|p.stock(L, W, T)                 # base block: x∈[0,L], y∈[0,W], z∈[0,T]. Exactly one per part, first call.
50|p.wall(edge, h, t=None)          # wall standing on the top face along a named edge, flush with that edge,
51|                                 # full edge length, height h above the stock top; t defaults to standard wall 2.5
52|p.boss(at=(x, y), dia, h)        # cylinder on the top face, centre at (x, y)
53|p.hole(code, at=(x, y))          # through hole (all the way down) using table KF; "-CB" adds the counterbore
54|p.pocket(at=(x, y), L, W, depth) # rectangular pocket from the top face; (x, y) = pocket's lower-left corner
55|p.slot(at=(x1, y1), to=(x2, y2), width, depth="thru")  # straight slot with round ends, centre line x1,y1→x2,y2
56|p.pattern(feature, nx, ny, dx, dy)   # repeat the LAST feature call nx × ny times with spacing dx, dy
57|p.fillet(edges="vertical", r=None)   # round the stock's 4 vertical outer edges; r defaults to standard 1.0
58|solid = p.finish()               # returns the CadQuery solid; must be the last call
59|```
60|- Errors are company-style and helpful (e.g. `KeelError: unknown fastener code 'M4'; use KF-M4`), because a real
61|  internal tool has its own error messages and the student must learn them too.
62|- `keel.render(p, path)` writes an SVG preview for the dashboard (CadQuery SVG export).
63|
64|### 3.4 What the answer looks like
65|The model writes a short Keel program ending in `solid = p.finish()`. The runner executes it and the referee compares
66|`solid` with the reference solid built by the job's own Keel reference program.
67|
68|## 4. The company manual (`company/manual.md`)
69|Written like a real internal wiki page: intro, conventions (3.1), table KF, every API call with one example each,
70|error messages, 3 worked examples. Target ≤ 4,000 tokens. It must contain **no** exam jobs.
71|
72|## 5. The internal dashboard (`company/dashboard/index.html`)
73|A static, **offline** web page (no CDN, no server, opens with a double-click; fits the "nothing leaves the building"
74|story). Reads `company/dashboard/data.json`, which a script (`company/dashboard/build_data.py`) creates from the
75|company files and Forge results. Look: a clean engineering intranet (dark navy + white, one accent colour), with the
76|"Fictional company" banner.
77|
78|Sections:
79|1. **Header**: Quillon Orbital Works · Engineering Portal · "QX-2 controlled: on-prem only" badge.
80|2. **Company**: what we build, the Petrel programmes, the teams (short cards).
81|3. **Tools**: Keel (version, link to the manual), Fastener table KF, Design rules, **Gauge** (the automatic checking
82|   station = our referee), **Forge assistant** (the on-prem AI). One card each: what it is, its status.
83|4. **Parts catalog**: grid of example parts (from practice families only, never exam jobs), each with its SVG
84|   preview, part number, Keel code (click to show) and key sizes.
85|5. **Design requests**: a table of requests with status: open / AI draft / Gauge PASS / Gauge FAIL (with reason:
86|   wrong shape, wrong position, error).
87|6. **Forge assistant panel**: where it runs (1 GPU, on-prem), the scoreboard (Glimmer + manual, Forge-trained
88|   Glimmer, teacher Spark Open) on the held-out exam, training status, cost. Shows "not measured yet" until results
89|   exist; never invented numbers.
90|
91|## 6. Acceptance checks (Muse Code must run them and report)
92|- `selftest`: every example part's Keel program builds exactly one valid solid; the referee scores every reference
93|  against itself PASS, and two deliberately wrong versions per example FAIL.
94|- Error messages: an unknown code, a second `stock()` call and a missing `finish()` each raise a clear `KeelError`.
95|- The dashboard opens offline (no network requests: grep for `http` in the HTML/JS = only text, no fetches to the web)
96|  and renders with the current `data.json`. Scoreboard shows "not measured yet" where there is no result file.
97|- No exam job text or exam part appears in the catalog, manual or examples (the exam is written later, separately).
98|
99|## 7. Not in this step
100|The 30-job held-out exam (written separately, frozen and blind-rebuilt as before), the practice generator, the
101|teacher run, training. Budget for this build: one Muse Code session, ~$0.50–0.80 Meta credit, user approval first.
